reviews.name: Mel
reviews.title: Director of Innovation · Greenlight Consulting
reviews.review_text: Highly recommend this course for anyone wanting to experience and understand what it's like to code using agents to support you in building what you envision. Carmelo's AAMAD framework is a step-by-step approach to translating a PRD into a working full-stack Crew AI agentic application. There's a lot of material covered, but you can always return for a deeper dive when you have more time. The framework itself is very structured: you build step by step using agents that take on the personas of a software delivery team. I'd definitely suggest completing the pre-course work — it prepares you well for the methodology and you learn how to use the agents and prompts within the AAMAD framework. I'd also recommend fully fleshing out your capstone PRD and MVP upfront so you don't spend too much time reworking things as you go. I haven't coded in a very long time, and I'm actually finding it very enjoyable now to build using AI. This course gave me a much better understanding of the shift in mindset required — and where to place your time and effort to get the most out of coding agents. If you have the time, you can even take your app all the way to production. Highly recommend. Thank you so much, Carmelo, for a really great learning experience!

reviews.name: Alberto
reviews.title: Cyberspace Technical Director · NATO
reviews.review_text: I have to say that this has been a wonderful journey. Many years ago, I developed safety-critical software using the waterfall approach and every possible engineering safeguard. On average, we produced around 8–10 lines of production code per day—including requirements, design, implementation, integration, testing, and documentation. A year ago, I started experimenting with vibe coding. It felt like stepping into a completely different world—a genuine paradigm shift that challenged everything I had learned about software engineering. Then AAMAD came to the rescue. AAMAD allows me to take full advantage of today's AI-assisted development tools while providing the process, structure, and engineering discipline needed to stay in control. It gives you visibility over the development process, the architecture, and the final product. Once you understand the underlying software engineering principles, AI stops feeling like a black box and becomes a powerful engineering tool. The definition of the AAMAD agents is particularly well thought out, enabling extremely rapid development without sacrificing structure or quality. The structure and pace of the course are equally impressive. Each phase builds naturally on the previous one, and you are encouraged to pause at key milestones to validate your work before moving forward. Along the way, you gain practical experience with concepts that have become essential for modern software engineering, including CI/CD, cloud deployment, observability, performance optimization, and token and cost management. This is not a course made of slides, nor one designed simply to tick a training box. It is a course to learn by building, to practice on a meaningful real-world project, and to grow as a software engineer. Looking back, the time, effort, and resources invested have been more than worthwhile. My sincere thanks and congratulations go to Carmelo Iaria for continuously keeping the learning materials current and relevant, for his daily engagement with the students, and for the encouragement, flexibility, and support he provided during the many occasions when I was unable to attend the live sessions. I also greatly appreciate the remarkable amount of additional material he shares with us beyond what was already a comprehensive course.

reviews.name: Aprill
reviews.title: Sr. UX Researcher · Cisco Systems, Inc.
reviews.review_text: Here's the same review with every `—` replaced: --- Carmelo Iaria's feedback on my capstone (an onboarding-plan tool built with CrewAI) was some of the most precise, actionable guidance I've gotten in a technical course. Early on, he caught that my architecture was solid but my task catalog was empty, and instead of just flagging it, he explained exactly why that mattered ("don't let the AI invent your company's real onboarding tasks") and gave me a clear, scoped next step: one role, one real catalog, one working demo before anything else.* *Throughout the build, his check-ins came at exactly the right moments, pushing for a UI when the CLI-only scope needed to grow, and trusting the architecture we'd already locked in rather than second-guessing it later. He has a rare combination of deep technical knowledge (CrewAI, agent architectures, production patterns) and genuine patience for students working through unfamiliar tools for the first time. I came out of this course with a fully working, tested, multi-agent application, and a much clearer sense of how to reason about AI system design, not just how to prompt an AI to build something. I HIGHLY recommend this course for others especially for people like me without a technical background [I am a UX Researcher not an engineer].
